question: UK: which documents legally control a stablecoin, digital gilt or tokenised fund, and which are still missing?
answer: Of 26 documents that control UK stablecoins, the digital gilt (DIGIT), tokenised funds and settlement (UK map, as of September 14, 2026), 10 are in force or final, 3 are drafts or open, and 13 are required but not published, not located or not yet inspected — among them the HSBC Gate 2 finality self-attestation, the DIGIT platform-provider appointment, the HSBC–LSEG bilateral DSD memorandum.

sections.title: Document by document
sections.sub: Grouped from public law down to correction and wind-down. Left out: 5 scenario-only documents (Territorial separation or reunification agreement; Implementing Acts and allocation schedules; Currency, central-bank and FMI continuity instruments; Private-contract and registry novations; Transition guarantees, resolution and dispute rules) and 10 roles the documents bind.

items.title: DSS Regulations 2023
kv: Sandbox entrants and in-scope connected DSS activity
Temporarily applies, disapplies or modifies specified legislation so DSD and related activities can occur.
Treasury report and any affirmative permanent amendments informed by the sandbox
Public full text and explanatory material
Modifications apply only within the DSS scope; non-DSS activity remains under the ordinary framework.

sources.label: Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 (Digital Securities Sandbox) Regulations 2023
Bank of England and FCA — Guidance on the operation of the Digital Securities Sandbox

items.title: HM Treasury systemic-recognition order
kv: Future gateway; no named operative order mapped
The legal person or payment system named in the eventual order
Would place a recognised systemic issuer or service within the Bank's statutory supervisory remit.
Published recognition order naming the exact issuer or system
Market size, an FCA authorisation or a company announcement does not itself create systemic recognition.

sources.label: Bank of England and FCA — joint systemic-stablecoin regulation

items.title: Bank DSS Rules Instrument 2024
kv: Current within DSS; firm-specific modifications possible
Sets requirements for notary, central maintenance, settlement, access, risk, outsourcing and other DSD functions.
Any amended instrument, Gate 3 rules and permanent-regime rules
General DSS rules can be modified by a firm-specific SAN; the applicable SAN may take precedence over guidance.

sources.label: Bank of England Digital Securities Sandbox Rules Instrument 2024
Bank of England and FCA — Guidance on the operation of the Digital Securities Sandbox
Bank of England–FCA Memorandum of Understanding for the Digital Securities Sandbox

items.title: Bank–FCA DSS Memorandum of Understanding
kv: Inter-regulator consultation, information sharing and coordination processes
Structures coordination over rules, SAN changes, supervision, enforcement, default, wind-down and emergency action.
Any amendment reflecting Gate 3 or a permanent regime
The advisory panel coordinates but does not take binding joint decisions; each regulator must act through its own governance.

sources.label: Bank of England–FCA Memorandum of Understanding for the Digital Securities Sandbox

items.title: HSBC Gate 2 Sandbox Approval Notice
kv: Bank of England; Bank and FCA for stated ancillary activities
Approves live notary, central-maintenance and settlement services for stated instruments and limits, plus listed ancillary activities and conditions.
Confirmed UK-government-debt limit, accepted finality self-attestation and any later SAN variation
The notice approves only listed activities. It does not remove other permissions or requirements and does not establish a completed DIGIT issuance.

sources.label: HSBC Bank plc — Gate 2 Sandbox Approval Notice, 13 July 2026
Bank of England — Digital Securities Sandbox dashboard

items.title: RTGS access policy
kv: Bank decision-making and applicant expectations rather than creating an account by itself
Distinguishes reserve, settlement-only, omnibus and prefunding routes and their eligibility criteria.
Synchronisation-operator access policy and firm-specific approval
Eligibility and policy do not create an account; contractual and operational requirements still must be met.

sources.label: Bank of England — Access policy for RTGS settlement accounts and services

items.title: FCA PS26/10 stablecoin-issuance rules
kv: Firms authorised for in-scope UK stablecoin issuance
Sets the qualifying-stablecoin issuance, backing, safeguarding, custody, redemption and disclosure framework.
First authorisations and product-specific disclosures under the effective regime
Public policy statements and Handbook materials
Final rules do not make a firm authorised before the regime applies and the firm receives the necessary authorisation.

sources.label: FCA — 2026 cryptoasset regime policy statements
Bank of England and FCA — joint systemic-stablecoin regulation

items.title: Bank systemic-stablecoin Code of Practice
kv: Would govern issuance, legal claim, redemption, backing assets, settlement access, capital, resilience and other systemic requirements.
Final Code of Practice and supporting 2027 materials
Public draft Code and policy statement
Draft rules and policy positions are not final binding requirements before finalisation and recognition of a firm.

sources.label: Bank of England — Sterling-denominated systemic stablecoins, June 2026
Bank of England and FCA — joint systemic-stablecoin regulation

items.title: FCA PS26/7 and COLL DLT-register guidance
kv: Authorised fund managers and depositaries through the existing framework
Explains how an on-chain DLT transaction record may serve as primary books and records for the register.
Named production fund documentation and correction evidence
Public policy statement and Handbook text
The guidance permits a DLT record to be primary; it does not relieve the responsible firm of register duties.

sources.label: FCA PS26/7 — Progressing fund tokenisation
FCA Handbook — COLL 6 Annex 4, use of DLT for authorised-fund registers

items.title: FCA–Bank FS26/1 wholesale-tokenisation feedback statement
kv: Published; implementation and consultation work remains future
FCA and Bank of England under separate mandates
No new general permission; records supervisory stance and future work relevant to regulated firms and infrastructures
Confirms regulated-firm accountability, records interim CASS 6 treatment for RSIC custody and sets work clocks for collateral, finality and custody.
Bank collateral eligibility terms, CCP supervisory material, the planned H1 2027 custody consultation and firm-specific operating receipts
Publication does not make a token eligible at the Bank or a CCP, authorise a firm, change CASS, create settlement finality or approve a product.

sources.label: FCA and Bank of England FS26/1 — Tokenisation in Wholesale Financial Markets
Bank of England and FCA — joint wholesale-tokenisation vision

items.title: FCA tokenised-gold Call for Input
kv: No product or firm; invites evidence and may inform later policy
Creates a formal inquiry record but no new product classification, permission, ownership rule, custody rule or collateral eligibility.
FCA response, consultation or final instrument plus product-specific title, custody, redemption and failure documents
The inquiry does not classify a token as direct bullion ownership, a fund, security, unallocated claim or cryptoasset; it grants no exemption, authorisation or collateral status.

sources.label: FCA — Tokenised Gold: Opportunities and Risks for UK Wholesale Markets
FCA and Bank of England FS26/1 — Tokenisation in Wholesale Financial Markets

items.title: DIGIT platform-provider appointment
kv: Award publicly announced; detailed contract not inspected
HM Treasury and the appointed HSBC contracting entity under the actual contract
Selects HSBC Orion as the platform path for the DIGIT pilot.
Executed issuance and service documents identifying obligations, service levels, liability and exit
Public award announcement; full contract not located
Provider appointment does not issue debt, determine investor title or complete settlement.

sources.label: HM Treasury — July 2026 DIGIT pilot update

items.title: HSBC–LSEG bilateral DSD memorandum
kv: Signed according to Treasury; operating agreement not located
The signatories only to the extent of the executed memorandum
Frames development of a bilateral DSD link with issuer-DSD and investor-DSD roles.
Executed link agreement, participant rules, record-priority terms, service levels and live transaction
Government summary; memorandum text not located
The memorandum does not itself prove production connectivity, interoperable title or settled investor access.

sources.label: HM Treasury — July 2026 DIGIT pilot update

items.title: RTGS legal-documentation suite
kv: RTGS account holders and payment-system operators under their signed terms
Creates the account and service relationship, supplemented by annexes and settlement-service or DvP agreements.
Public route; some downloadable legal documents and participant materials
RTGS Rules explain and elaborate the suite but do not override the operative contractual documents.

sources.label: Bank of England — Payment and settlement legal-documentation route
Bank of England — RTGS Rules version 2.1, March 2026

items.title: RTGS Rules version 2.1
kv: Sets access criteria, risk-management expectations, information duties and actions the Bank may take when concerned.
Any version adding live synchronisation requirements
The plain-language rules do not replace participant agreements, the CHAPS Reference Manual or system-specific settlement agreements.

sources.label: Bank of England — RTGS Rules version 2.1, March 2026

items.title: Bank synchronisation legal terms
items.sub: Future public-operator contract and access terms
kv: Future synchronisation operators and RTGS account holders
Would grant and condition access to RT2 synchronisation functions and the permitted use of RTGS earmarks.
Published terms, regulatory-status decision and first executed operator agreement
Future scene-setting and legal documentation anticipated
Working-group discussion and a lab do not establish the operative terms or regulatory status of synchronisation operators.

sources.label: Bank of England — Synchronisation thematic working-group minutes, 30 April 2026
Bank of England — Synchronisation roles and permissions
Bank of England — Synchronisation Lab

items.title: Synchronisation-operator participant rulebook
kv: Each synchronisation operator with its participants
Only parties to the relevant operator arrangement
Would govern instructions, permissions, sequencing, data, fees, liability, default and exit below the Bank layer.
Named operator, published rulebook or executed participant agreement
The Bank has stated that detailed rulebooks and terms would be managed by operators with participants; no universal executed rulebook exists at cutoff.

sources.label: Bank of England — Synchronisation thematic working-group minutes, 30 April 2026

items.title: DLT register-governance procedure
kv: Required where DLT is used; product specific
Technology providers, delegates and users through incorporated terms
Specifies valid writers, identity checks, access, data, record precedence and reconciliation for the operative register.
Named fund procedure and operational audit
Consensus validates network instructions; the responsible firm retains the legal duty to keep the register complete and current.

sources.label: FCA Handbook — COLL 6 Annex 4, use of DLT for authorised-fund registers

items.title: DIGIT operative issuance-document set
items.sub: Sovereign issuance and market document bundle
kv: Required; not yet published or executed at cutoff
HM Treasury/DMO with appointed market institutions
Issuer, DSDs, dealers, custodians and investors according to the final documents
Would create the debt obligation and identify the authoritative record, settlement asset, transfer rules and investor rights.
Final terms, closing documents, listing documents and first settlement receipt
No completed issuance set at cutoff
Announced design features and target timing are not the executed legal terms of a gilt.

sources.label: HM Treasury — July 2026 DIGIT pilot update
HSBC Bank plc — Gate 2 Sandbox Approval Notice, 13 July 2026

items.title: Synchronisation customer mandate
kv: Required by the published role model; specimen not published
Account holder, customer and synchronisation operator
The contracting parties and permitted transaction types
Would authorise the operator to act for the customer while preserving account-holder and ledger controls.
Named live use case and executed terms
A customer can choose an operator and transaction type only within the permissions of the account holder, Bank and external ledger.

sources.label: Bank of England — Synchronisation roles and permissions

items.title: Stablecoin trust, custody and holder-contract stack
kv: Required by the regime; no named authorised UK product mapped
Only the named product's parties and beneficiaries
Creates the redemption obligation, backing-asset trust and custody/control structure through which holder rights are enforced.
First authorised issuer's final terms, trust instrument, custody agreement and disclosures
No complete named UK-authorised specimen at cutoff
A generic white paper or reserve attestation is not the full enforceable trust, custody and holder-contract stack.

sources.label: FCA — 2026 cryptoasset regime policy statements
Bank of England — Sterling-denominated systemic stablecoins, June 2026
Bank of England and FCA — joint systemic-stablecoin regulation

items.title: Tokenised-fund scheme-document stack
kv: Required for each fund; specimens are product specific
Authorised fund manager with depositary and appointed providers
The fund, providers and investors under the exact documents
Defines the unit, responsible roles, dealing, valuation, custody, transfer, redemption and governance around the DLT register.
Named tokenised fund's complete current scheme and service set
Token standards or wallet terms cannot silently override the scheme instrument or investor rights.

sources.label: FCA PS26/7 — Progressing fund tokenisation
FCA Handbook — COLL 6 Annex 4, use of DLT for authorised-fund registers

items.title: HSBC Gate 2 finality self-attestation
kv: Required by SAN; acceptance not publicly established
HSBC Bank plc; reviewed by Bank of England
HSBC's Gate 2 activity as a condition of approval
Addresses the settlement-finality proposals on which live DSD activity depends.
Bank confirmation that the condition is satisfied and the operative finality analysis
Requirement public; underlying submission not located
The SAN's requirement proves the document is required; it does not prove acceptance or disclose its legal analysis.

sources.label: HSBC Bank plc — Gate 2 Sandbox Approval Notice, 13 July 2026

items.title: Cross-ledger finality and failure terms
kv: Material design gap; no reconciled operative set published
Bank, synchronisation operator, asset-ledger operator and participants by instrument
Each party under its applicable document
Must identify finality, timeouts, cancellation, correction, recovery, liability and dispute hierarchy across both legs.
Live rulebooks plus a legal-finality opinion and tested failure receipt
No complete public cross-document set located
Technical atomicity does not by itself answer which legal event is final or who pays when the two ledgers disagree.

sources.label: Bank of England — Synchronisation roles and permissions
Bank of England — Synchronisation thematic working-group minutes, 30 April 2026
Bank of England — RTGS Rules version 2.1, March 2026

items.title: Stablecoin wind-down and insolvency document set
kv: Rule-required future firm documentation; no stressed case proven
Issuer and fiduciaries under FCA/Bank supervision
Issuer, service providers and claimants according to law and contract
Must govern reconciliation, redemption suspension or continuation, asset realisation, portability, insolvency and loss allocation.
Approved wind-down plan and observed recovery or insolvency treatment
No named authorised UK stablecoin set at cutoff
A 1:1 backing claim in ordinary operation does not by itself prove timing, priority or recovery in insolvency.

sources.label: FCA — 2026 cryptoasset regime policy statements
Bank of England — Sterling-denominated systemic stablecoins, June 2026
Bank of England and FCA — joint systemic-stablecoin regulation

items.title: DLT register-correction authority
kv: The register operation and delegated technology arrangements
Preserves the responsible firm's ability to reverse incorrect entries or create necessary corrective entries.
Tested correction receipt and governance log for a named production fund
Rule public; firm implementation product specific
The correction power must not require third-party consent, apart from normal network consensus validating authorised instructions.

sources.label: FCA Handbook — COLL 6 Annex 4, use of DLT for authorised-fund registers

uncertain: This layer maps published controlling instruments and explicitly identified future document classes. An enacted framework, regulator guidance, sandbox approval, memorandum, draft rule, private contract and scenario-only transition instrument have different legal effects and clocks. Unpublished or future documents are not treated as operative.
'Missing or not public' groups documents the overlay calls required, future, under design, not published or not located; each card prints the overlay's own words.
